chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal who said:

I asked al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah — 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth' [24:35] — so he said: '(He is) a Guide for the inhabitants of the sky, and a Guide for the inhabitants of the earth.'
And in the narration of al-Barqi: '(He is) Guidance for those in the sky and Guidance for those in the earth.'

key_terms.نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: Light of the heavens and the earth — the divine epithet from Quran 24:35 (Ayat al-Nur)
key_terms.هَادٍ: Guide — an active participle form indicating one who continuously guides
key_terms.هُدَى: Guidance — an alternative reading/wording in al-Barqi's narration, emphasizing the result rather than the agent

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha (AS) say about the meaning of 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth' (Quran 24:35)?
ai.summary: This hadith records al-Abbas ibn Hilal's question to Imam Ali al-Ridha (AS), the eighth Imam, regarding the famous Ayat al-Nur (Verse of Light, Quran 24:35). The Imam explains the Divine Name 'Light' (Nur) in functional terms: Allah is a Guide (Hadin) for the denizens of the heavens and the earth. An alternate wording preserved from al-Barqi's narration uses 'Guidance' (Huda) instead of 'Guide,' emphasizing that the divine light encompasses all creation in its guiding role. This exegesis reflects the Shia theological method of interpreting divine attributes through their practical, cosmological effects on creation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Al Abbas Bin Hilal who said,

‘I asked Al-Rezaasws about the Words of Allahazwj [24:35] Allah is Light of the skies and the earth. So heasws said: ‘A Guide for the inhabitants of the sky and a Guide for the inhabitants of the earth’.
And in a report of Al-Barqy, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘A Guidance for the ones in the sky and a Guidance for the ones in the earth’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from al-‘Abbass ibn Hilal who has said the following.

“I asked Imam al-Rida (a.s.), about the words of Allah, ‘Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth’” [24:35]. The Imam replied, “Allah is the Guide for all that is in the heavens and the Guide for all that is on the earth.”
According to another Hadith narrated by al-Barqi,(the Imam said), “Allah has guided everyone in the heavens and every one on the earth.”
